answer: Resist sybils with synchronous co-presence rounds: each epoch every identity, a vertex in the participation graph, is randomly paired to bridge live with a peer for a short seed-derived exchange nobody can precompute. A sybil farmer's whole edge is asynchronous multiplexing — one model behind a thousand identities. Forced live in many simultaneous slots, one operator must buy genuine concurrent attention per head, so cost scales with headcount, and correlated latencies across heads form a nebula of timing fingerprints exposing shared origin — expensive or self-revealing.
